# Issaquah Dispatch

> The Issaquah Dispatch is a free weekly email newsletter about Issaquah, WA, sent Thursdays at 6 AM Pacific and published by Neighborhood Press LLC. It covers city council decisions, land-use and permit notices, road and transit changes, school district news, openings and closings, with one section per neighborhood. Every item links its public source. It is researched and written with AI tools, and an editor reads every issue before it goes out.

## Key pages
- [This week in Issaquah](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/this-week/): the dated items for the current week, updated every Thursday
- [Issaquah news](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/news/): every story, newest first
- [Reader asked](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/asked/): readers' questions answered from the public record
- [Standards](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/standards/): publisher, sources, sponsors, corrections
- [Subscribe](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/): free, one email a week

## Neighborhoods
- [Central Issaquah](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/central-issaquah/): The valley floor along I-90 and Gilman Boulevard, with Gilman Village, the big employers and the Central Issaquah plan reshaping the shopping centers.
- [Issaquah Highlands](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/issaquah-highlands/): The urban village on Grand Ridge above I-90: Blakely Hall, Grand Ridge Plaza, the park-and-ride and trails into Grand Ridge Park.
- [Issaquah Valley](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/issaquah-valley/): The valley at the foot of Squak Mountain beside Olde Town, with Confluence Park, Berntsen Park and Salmon Run Park.
- [Montreux](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/montreux/): The wooded northern slope of Cougar Mountain, looking out over Lake Sammamish toward the Cascades.
- [Newport](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/newport/): West of SR 900 and south of I-90, where Newport Way crosses Tibbetts Creek near Tibbetts Valley Park and the Cougar Mountain trailhead.
- [North Issaquah](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/north-issaquah/): The valley floor north of I-90, next to Lake Sammamish State Park and the East Lake Sammamish Trail.
- [Olde Town](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/olde-town/): Issaquah's historic downtown: Front Street, the Issaquah Depot, Village Theatre, the salmon hatchery and the Issaquah Creek trail.
- [Providence Point](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/providence-point/): 161 rolling acres in the Cascade foothills above Lake Sammamish, bordered by Laughing Jacobs Creek, with miles of walking paths.
- [South Lake Sammamish](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/south-lake-sammamish/): The southwest end of Lake Sammamish, with Timberlake Park, Blackberry Park and Meerwood Park along the shore.
- [Squak Mountain](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/squak-mountain/): The mountain closest to downtown, with towering evergreens and the trails of Squak Mountain State Park.
- [Sycamore](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/sycamore/): Both sides of Front Street South at the city's southern edge, between Tiger and Squak mountains, with Issaquah Creek, Squak Valley Park and the Poo Poo Point trailhead.
- [Talus](https://www.issaquahdispatch.com/talus/): The hillside community on Cougar Mountain, with Harvey Manning Park and trail access into the Issaquah Alps.
